strategy_title: Coalesced Transpose via Tile Swap and tl.trans()
strategy_description: When a Triton transpose kernel loads with a large stride between consecutive warp threads (e.g., stride-N in source layout), L1 hit rate collapses to 0% and L2 saturates near 100%. Swapping the tile orientation so that the load dimension spans the stride-1 axis of the source (making loads coalesced), then using tl.trans() to reorder the in-register tile before storing coalesced to the destination, converts strided memory transactions into 128-byte coalesced accesses. This reduced L2 throughput from 96.92% to 59.13%, raised L1 hit rate from 0% to 53.93%, and cut warp stall cycles per instruction from 74 to 40, yielding a 1.22x speedup.
slow_pseudocode:
# Non-coalesced: consecutive threads differ in spatial index (stride 128 in src)
yindex = pid_y * YBLOCK + arange(YBLOCK)[:, None]  # [YBLOCK, 1]
xindex = pid_x * XBLOCK + arange(XBLOCK)[None, :]  # [1, XBLOCK]
c = yindex % 128; b = yindex // 128
# Load: src addr = c + 128*xindex + 4032000*b  => stride-128 between threads
tile = load(in_ptr + c + 128*xindex + 4032000*b, mask=xmask, eviction_policy='evict_last')  # [YBLOCK, XBLOCK]
store(out_ptr + xindex + 31500*yindex, tile, mask=xmask)
fast_pseudocode:
# Coalesced: swap tile orientation so threads span stride-1 axis on load
rows = pid_y * YBLOCK + arange(YBLOCK)   # [YBLOCK]: channel/batch index
cols = pid_x * XBLOCK + arange(XBLOCK)   # [XBLOCK]: spatial index
c = rows % 128; b = rows // 128
# Load [XBLOCK, YBLOCK]: threads span YBLOCK (channel, stride-1 in src) => COALESCED
src = c[None, :] + 128 * cols[:, None] + 4032000 * b[None, :]  # [XBLOCK, YBLOCK]
tile = load(in_ptr + src, mask=col_mask[:,None] & row_mask[None,:])  # [XBLOCK, YBLOCK]
# Store [YBLOCK, XBLOCK]: threads span XBLOCK (spatial, stride-1 in dst) => COALESCED
dst = cols[None, :] + 31500 * rows[:, None]  # [YBLOCK, XBLOCK]
store(out_ptr + dst, tl.trans(tile), mask=row_mask[:,None] & col_mask[None,:])
# tl.trans() is a register-level shuffle: [XBLOCK, YBLOCK] -> [YBLOCK, XBLOCK], no shared memory needed
# Wrap kernel with @triton.autotune over YBLOCK/XBLOCK tile shapes and num_stages
applicable_when: L1/TEX hit rate is 0% or near 0%; L2 cache throughput is >80%; CPIStall rule fires with >40% of cycles stalled on L1TEX scoreboard; kernel is a layout permutation/transpose where the source tensor has stride-1 along a dimension that is NOT the innermost thread dimension in the current tiling; DRAM throughput is high relative to compute throughput.
do_not_apply_when: The kernel is already compute-bound (Compute SM Throughput >60%); the source tensor's stride-1 dimension is already aligned with the innermost thread dimension (loads are already coalesced); tl.trans() is unavailable or the tile dimensions are not powers of 2; the transpose involves more than 2 dimensions requiring a more complex shared-memory tiling approach.
framework_notes: tl.trans() in Triton performs a register-level 2D tile transpose ([M, N] -> [N, M]) without explicit shared memory allocation, making it efficient for in-register data reordering. The equivalent in CUDA would require shared memory tiling with padding to avoid bank conflicts. @triton.autotune with key=['ynumel', 'xnumel'] allows the runtime to select the best YBLOCK/XBLOCK combination and num_stages for the target hardware.
